newsitem.title: UK: Railtrack drops on windfall tax fears.
newsitem.headline: Railtrack drops on windfall tax fears.

text.p: Shares in Railtrack Plc plummeted in pre-market trade on Monday, after a report that the company could be among the biggest victims of the government's planned windfall tax on privatised utilities.
The stock was down 25p at 629-1/2 by 0726 GMT in volume of 420,300 shares.
The Sunday Telegraph said the government was planning to levy a windfall tax of 500 million stg on Railtrack, the heaviest on any privatised company, arguing it was sold off too cheaply in 1996.
"At the moment, it's pure speculation if they are subject to the windfall tax", one analyst said, "but after last weeks comments and the renewed speculation it's more likely than before".

Last week, Britain's rail watchdog said it was poised to set out "clear, fair, achievable objectives" for the privatised rail operators as it would not be longer sufficient to provide only bare minimum services.

This came in the wake of a statement of Deputy Prime Minister John Prescott, who indicated earlier this month Railtrack faced tougher treatment that could come in the form of windfall taxes, fines and tougher sanctions.
